title: Consume bisected selector prefixes before residual filtering
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView.select() already proves a contiguous leading selector prefix by bisecting the canonical SparseTensorEntry order, but it then retained those same prefix predicates in the normalized selector map and re-read them for every candidate inside the narrowed range. Prefix predicates therefore incurred duplicate per-entry coordinate work after the binary-search bounds had already established them.
primary_claim: TensorView.select() now consumes validated leading selector predicates while building the bisect prefix, leaving only genuinely residual non-prefix predicates for per-entry filtering. Prefix-only selection retains the existing bounded bisect entry access and no longer rechecks the proven prefix coordinate on every retained candidate.
gardener_decision: Reuse the existing normalized selector dictionary rather than adding a second residual-selector structure. Pop each contiguous leading selector as it is copied into the canonical bisect prefix; the existing matching loop then sees only non-prefix predicates. Do not add an index, cache, planner or alternate selection abstraction.
